_comment: Reference list of Living-Off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBins) commonly abused for execution, defense evasion, and persistence. Risk levels reflect typical abuse frequency, not intrinsic maliciousness -- all of these are legitimate OS binaries.

binaries.name: powershell.exe
binaries.notes: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell. Encoded (-enc) or hidden-window (-w hidden) invocations are a strong abuse signal.

binaries.name: mshta.exe
binaries.notes: Signed Binary Proxy Execution via HTA. Frequently used to execute remote scripts while evading application allowlisting.

binaries.name: rundll32.exe
binaries.notes: Signed Binary Proxy Execution. Commonly abused to load malicious DLLs under a trusted process name.

binaries.name: regsvr32.exe
binaries.notes: Signed Binary Proxy Execution ('Squiblydoo'). Can register/execute scriptlets fetched from a remote URL.

binaries.name: certutil.exe
binaries.notes: Legitimate certificate utility frequently repurposed to download or base64-decode payloads.

binaries.name: wmic.exe
binaries.notes: Windows Management Instrumentation. Used for remote execution, discovery, and occasionally persistence.

binaries.name: schtasks.exe
binaries.notes: Scheduled Task/Job. A very common persistence mechanism for re-launching a payload on a timer.

binaries.name: psexec.exe
binaries.notes: Legitimate Sysinternals tool for remote execution, widely abused for lateral movement post-compromise.

binaries.name: bitsadmin.exe
binaries.notes: BITS Jobs. Used to stage downloads that persist across reboots and evade some network monitoring.
